image.style: clean flat vector schematic illustration, thin dark outlines (#33475B), flat fills, textbook diagram look, no photorealism, no shadows
image.overall: Two separate circuit illustrations side by side, occupying the left half and the right half of the frame, with a clear vertical gap of empty white between them and no dividing line. Each illustration is a simple closed rectangular wire loop drawn with clean right-angled corners. LEFT LOOP: a battery pack on the left side of the loop, a zig-zag resistor symbol on the top wire, and a small red LED symbol (triangle with a bar) on the right side of the loop. RIGHT LOOP: the same battery pack on the left side of an otherwise completely bare rectangular wire loop -- no resistor, no LED, nothing but wire. The wire of the right-hand loop should be tinted with a warm orange-red glow (#E74C3C at low opacity) spreading outward from the wire to suggest heat, strongest along the top and right segments. The left-hand loop's wire is plain dark grey with no glow.
image.layoutNotes: Each loop should occupy roughly 38% of the total frame width and 55% of the frame height, vertically centred. Leave at least 8% clear white margin around the outside of each loop and a clear 10% gap between them. Do not draw any numbers, voltage values, current values, ammeters, or component value markings -- those are all added by the overlay. Do not draw a divider, caption, or heading between or above the two loops.

callouts.label: 6V battery pack
callouts.hint: The power source on the left side of the left-hand loop.
callouts.description: The same 6 volt supply feeds both circuits. Nothing about the battery changes between them -- only what the current has to pass through.

draw.position: On the left vertical wire of the LEFT-hand loop, about 13% from the left and 50% from the top.
draw.visual: A standard battery symbol: alternating long thin and short thick horizontal plates, drawn across the left vertical wire of the loop.

callouts.label: 220-ohm resistor
callouts.hint: A zig-zag symbol on the top wire of the left-hand loop only.
callouts.description: The current-limiting resistor. It is the only thing standing between the battery and a very large current, and it is exactly what the short circuit on the right is missing.

draw.position: On the top horizontal wire of the LEFT-hand loop, about 27% from the left and 23% from the top.
draw.visual: A classic zig-zag resistor symbol with six peaks, drawn inline in the top wire, with a small tan-coloured body if the style calls for it.

callouts.label: ~27 mA (safe)
callouts.hint: The right side of the left-hand loop, where the light-emitting component sits.
callouts.description: With 6 V across a 220 ohm resistor and an LED, roughly 27 milliamps flows. That is inside what a standard LED tolerates, so the parts stay cool.

draw.position: On the right vertical wire of the LEFT-hand loop, about 40% from the left and 50% from the top, at the LED symbol.
draw.visual: A red LED schematic symbol: a triangle pointing down into a horizontal bar, with two small arrows radiating away from it to indicate emitted light.

callouts.label: ~6 A (dangerous, gets hot)
callouts.hint: The bare wire loop on the right, glowing warm.
callouts.description: With the resistor and LED removed, only the wire's own tiny resistance limits the current. Six volts across a fraction of an ohm is amps, not milliamps, and all of that energy becomes heat in the wire and the battery.

draw.position: On the right vertical wire of the RIGHT-hand loop, about 75% from the left and 50% from the top, in the middle of the glowing bare wire.
draw.visual: Plain bare wire with no component interrupting it, surrounded by a soft warm orange-red heat glow that fades outward.
